title: Russian forces open an offensive in northern Kharkiv Oblast
body:
On 10 May 2024 Russian forces attacked across the border into Kharkiv Oblast in northeastern Ukraine. The attack proceeded along two axes: one toward Vovchansk and one toward Lyptsi, north of Kharkiv city. Roughly four to five Russian infantry battalions led the initial armoured assault. A senior Ukrainian military source told Reuters that Russia aimed to advance up to 10 kilometres to create a buffer zone, and Russian military bloggers later cited 15 kilometres. Ukrainian officials did not believe Russia could capture Kharkiv city.

Ukrainian forces were already stretched along a front of more than 1,000 kilometres. Kharkiv's governor reported that more than 10,500 residents had been evacuated from the affected areas by 20 May 2024, and by 14 May only about 400 civilians remained in Vovchansk. Russia captured several border villages and parts of Vovchansk but did not advance further.

By 23 and 24 May Ukraine said the Russian advance had been halted in the Lyptsi direction, and by 1 June Russian bloggers described the offensive as stalled. In late May 2024, announced on 30 May, US President Joe Biden permitted Ukraine to use US-supplied weapons against targets in Russia near Kharkiv Oblast, and Germany, France and the United Kingdom gave similar permission.
